title: Frontend: Shortest Distance from Source (Bellman-Ford Algorithm)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Shortest Distance from Source (Bellman-Ford Algorithm). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges,source}) for directed weighted edges, allowing negative weights. Return source distances with null for unreachable. Throw Negative cycle only when a negative cycle is reachable from source.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Initialize the source to zero and other distances to infinity.
alternativeApproaches: Propagate an unbounded marker to every vertex reachable from a detected negative cycle.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Negative edge; unreachable component; early stop.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
